technique_agent_architecture.answer:
Based on GitHub evidence from active developer communities, **Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and harness-based agent architecture are the dominant emerging patterns**, with practical implementations prioritizing structured context management and skill modularization over monolithic agent designs.

## Model Context Protocol as Infrastructure Layer

The **affaan-m/everything-claude-code** repository (83,114 stars, 1,408.4★/day velocity)[1] represents the highest-signal implementation pattern. Rather than treating MCP as optional, developers are building it as the foundational abstraction layer for agent communication. The repository demonstrates MCP-driven discovery where agents dynamically load capabilities instead of relying on static tool definitions[1][7].

**Context-Engine** (242 stars)[1] exemplifies this with a production-oriented MCP retrieval stack combining hybrid code search (dense + lexical + reranking), ReFRAG micro-chunking, and local LLM prompt enhancement—deployed across Cursor, Windsurf, Roo, and Cline. This shows the shift from "agents talking to APIs" toward "agents discovering and negotiating protocol-standardized tools."

## Harness Engineering: Structure Over Speed

The critical friction point developers report: **Claude Code writes code fast but without structure, it skips tests, loses context, and produces inconsistent results—especially on complex, multi-step problems**[6]. This directly contradicts the "faster iteration" narrative.
